title: Unchangeable Scrolls
description: Learn about Tuples: the magical unchangeable scrolls that look like lists but lock their values forever!

content.value: Lists are great because we can change them, append items, or delete items. But what if we want to store a list of things that should NEVER change? Like the coordinates of a treasure chest or the months of the year? For that, we use Tuples! Tuples are like ancient, magical scrolls: once you write something on them, it is locked forever.
We write tuples using regular parentheses `( )` instead of square brackets `[ ]`.
If you try to change a tuple after creating it, Python will protect it and raise an error. This is a super useful feature to make sure your important data doesn't get messed up by accident!

coords = (10, 20)
# coords[0] = 5   # If you run this, Python will crash with a TypeError!

quiz.question: What punctuation marks are used to create a Tuple?
quiz.explain: Tuples are made with parentheses `( )`. Square brackets make lists and curly brackets make dictionaries/sets.

quiz.question: Can you add or modify items in a Tuple after creating it?
quiz.explain: Tuples are immutable -- once created they can't be changed, so there's no append() for them.
